body:
Depends very much on the plugin magic being done. Since you can reproduce it consistently but can't narrow down the steps, could you try bisecting (start with 0.1.7, if it happens there, we'll assume it's an old bug. But if it doesn't happen there, and can be bisected to something since 0.1.7, that will help a lot.)

This looks similar to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/6004 but I can't imagine why the plugin would be switching between buffers for the steps you describe. Anyways, could be worth trying `:set hidden` if you don't already have that set.

This crash is reproducible on `v0.1.7` and `:set nohidden` does not appear to help.

Thanks

And it's definitely the rust syntax highlight plugin causing the issue.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust.vim

I can't reproduce it locally.

```sh
$ git clone https://github.com/rust-lang/rust.vim
...
$ nvim -u NONE --cmd 'set rtp+=rust.vim' --cmd 'syn on' main.rs
```

Can you give steps from a basic setup like above to produce this?

I was unable to repro using a command like the one above.

But this works:

* blast plugin dir to start afresh

 * In init.vim only these three lines:
```
call plug#begin('~/.vim/plugged')
Plug 'rust-lang/rust.vim'
call plug#end()
```

 * `:PlugInstall`

* Using this file:
  https://gist.github.com/vext01/c3436a521af1929ad75e5d48495ca0fe

* Open in nvim

* Scroll to line 166 and position cursor on closing brace of `fn render_node` function.

* Type `o<cr>fn`

* Vim crashes consistently on pressing the last `n`

issue.body:
Oni frequent crash on Windows 7,  such as the following scenario will crash:

*  enter dd  consecutively to delete text line.

* quick open file.

Oni version:
```sh
* fa8a529 (HEAD -> master, origin/master, origin/HEAD) Fix #407, use editor.quickOpen.execCommand to filter files in qui
ckOpen (#489)
```

body:
I have the exact same issue as vext01 - crashing while editing a rust file and trying to add a new function after opening a new line. I can reproduce in neovim and in vim8.

The relevant section from the core dump / disassembly is 

```
   0x00001c7ad2fe9ba6 <+3878>:  cmp    QWORD PTR [rip+0x31db2a],0x0        # 0x1c7ad33076d8 <current_next_list>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bae <+3886>:  je     0x1c7ad2fe9be7 <syn_current_attr+3943>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bb0 <+3888>:  mov    rdi,QWORD PTR [rip+0x31da99]        # 0x1c7ad3307650 <syn_buf>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bb7 <+3895>:  mov    rsi,QWORD PTR [rip+0x31daa2]        # 0x1c7ad3307660 <current_lnum>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bbe <+3902>:  xor    edx,edx
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bc0 <+3904>:  call   0x1c7ad2f0c770 <ml_get_buf>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bc5 <+3909>:  mov    ecx,DWORD PTR [rip+0x31daad]        # 0x1c7ad3307678 <current_col>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bcb <+3915>:  inc    ecx
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bcd <+3917>:  movsxd rcx,ecx
=> 0x00001c7ad2fe9bd0 <+3920>:  cmp    BYTE PTR [rax+rcx*1],0x0
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bd4 <+3924>:  jne    0x1c7ad2fe9be7 <syn_current_attr+3943>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bd6 <+3926>:  movzx  eax,WORD PTR [rip+0x31db07]        # 0x1c7ad33076e4 <current_next_flags>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bdd <+3933>:  test   ax,0x280
   0x00001c7ad2fe9be1 <+3937>:  je     0x1c7ad2fe9c75 <syn_current_attr+4085>
   0x00001c7ad2fe9be7 <+3943>:  cmp    DWORD PTR [rbp-0x288],0x0
   0x00001c7ad2fe9bee <+3950>:  jle    0x1c7ad2fe9bfc <syn_current_attr+3964>

```

Which I think corresponds to line 2136 from src/nvim/syntax.c (note that syn_getcurline() has been inlined to just be a call to `ml_get_buf(syn_buf, current_lnum, FALSE);`):

```
  if (current_next_list != NULL
      && syn_getcurline()[current_col + 1] == NUL
      && !(current_next_flags & (HL_SKIPNL | HL_SKIPEMPTY)))
current_next_list = NULL;
```

The crash is happening while trying to get the value of `syn_getcurline()[current_col + 1] `. When I look at the register values it looks like %rax is pointing to the end of an allocated region: 

```
(gdb) info reg
rax            0x1c7d107d5fff   31323473141759
rcx            0x1      1
...
(gdb) x/bx $rax
```
